title: Simple Bruhat double-coset multiplication
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $G$ be a semisimple simply connected $F$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme]: smooth, connected, affine and of finite type with no nontrivial smooth connected solvable normal subgroup, and with every surjective homomorphism from a semisimple group having finite central kernel an isomorphism. Solvable means that successive scheme-theoretic commutator subgroups become trivial, and central means commuting after every scalar extension. Fix a split maximal torus $T\subseteq B\subseteq G$, with $B$ a Borel subgroup, and use $Q=G/B$, the roots $\Phi$, positive roots $\Phi^+$ and simple roots $\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_r$ of [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure]. Put $W=N_G(T)(F)/T(F)$ and choose representatives $n_w$ as in [lem-sfb-bruhat-longest-cell-charts]. Write $s_i=s_{\alpha_i}$ for the reflections of [lem-sfb-reductive-rank-one-reflections], and $\ell(w)$ for the minimum number of simple reflections with product $w$. For every algebraically closed extension $K/F$ put $D_w(K)=B(K)n_wB(K)\subseteq G(K)$. Products of subsets mean $A A\prime=\{aa\prime:a\in A,a\prime\in A\prime\}$. For every $i$ and $w\in W$ one has $D_{s_i}(K)D_w(K)=D_{s_iw}(K)$ if $\ell(s_iw)=\ell(w)+1$, and $D_{s_i}(K)D_w(K)=D_{s_iw}(K)\cup D_w(K)$ if $\ell(s_iw)=\ell(w)-1$. These are the only two possible length cases. For any nonempty reduced expression $w=s_{i_1}\cdots s_{i_m}$ it follows that $D_{s_{i_1}}(K)\cdots D_{s_{i_m}}(K)=D_w(K)$. There is no characteristic restriction; the empty reduced word represents $1$ and $D_1(K)=B(K)$.

source.place: Milne iAG2017 Proposition 21.75 (T3), printed p.448, and rank-one root-group calculation; Brion--Kumar Section 2.1 equation (4), printed p.62, including the paragraph on reduced products at the start of Section 2.2, p.64. Primary author-hosted PDF read online; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure], semisimplicity implies reductivity. By [lem-sfb-weyl-reflection-realization], $W$ acts faithfully on $E=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbf Q}\Phi$ and equals its root-reflection group. Extend $E$ to $E_{\mathbf R}$ and average any positive definite inner product over finite $W$. Every $s_\alpha$ is then orthogonal: its $+1$ hyperplane is perpendicular to its $-1$ line $\mathbf R\alpha$, so its given coroot formula is the orthogonal reflection formula. The simple roots are a real basis of $E_{\mathbf R}$ by their rational independence and the integral sign expansions in the Borel-pair statement. Thus [lem-sfb-simple-root-reflection-generation] says every $w$ has a simple-reflection word; its least length exists. For simple $\alpha$, the reflection changes only the $\alpha$ coefficient of a root's simple-root expansion. A positive root $\beta\ne\alpha$ has a positive coefficient elsewhere (reducedness excludes other multiples of $\alpha$), hence $s_\alpha\beta$ is positive and differs from $\alpha$. Since $s_\alpha^2=1$, it permutes $\Phi^+\setminus\{\alpha\}$.

Fix $s=s_\alpha$. Reversing a word shows $\ell(w^{-1})=\ell(w)$, and appending $s$ shows $|\ell(sw)-\ell(w)|\le1$. If $w^{-1}\alpha$ is negative, apply [lem-sfb-root-sign-word-deletion] to a shortest word for $w^{-1}$ and the positive root $\alpha$. The preceding step verified its sign-partition and simple-reflection hypotheses. Deleting one letter gives a word of length $\ell(w)-1$ for $w^{-1}s$, so $\ell(sw)=\ell(w)-1$. If $w^{-1}\alpha$ is positive, $(sw)^{-1}\alpha=-w^{-1}\alpha$ is negative. Apply the just proved implication to $sw$, obtaining $\ell(w)=\ell(sw)-1$. Thus precisely the stated two cases occur, and they correspond respectively to positive and negative $w^{-1}\alpha$. This also treats $w=1$.

source.place: Appendix C.10--C.11, p.610; explicit exchange-to-length argument.

proof.text: Work on $K$-points. By [lem-sfb-reductive-root-subgroup-parametrizations], conjugation by any $n_w$ sends $U_\beta$ onto $U_{w\beta}$: the conjugate is smooth connected, is normalized by $T$, and has tangent weight $w\beta$, so uniqueness in that statement applies. Its torus-action formula holds over every $F$-algebra, hence over $K$. Choose $v_\alpha$ from [lem-sfb-opposite-root-sl2-parametrizations], and put $u_\pm(a)=v_\alpha(x_\pm(a))$, $h(a)=v_\alpha(\operatorname{diag}(a,a^{-1}))$ and $n=v_\alpha(\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&-1\\1&0\end{smallmatrix}\right))$. Matrix multiplication gives $n=x_+(-1)x_-(1)x_+(-1)$ before applying $v_\alpha$. The torus-action formula on $u_\pm$ therefore gives $tnt^{-1}=h(\alpha(t))n$. Hence $ntn^{-1}=t h(\alpha(t))^{-1}$; on characters this is $\chi\mapsto\chi-\langle\chi,\alpha^\vee\rangle\alpha$, so $n$ represents $s$ by faithfulness in [lem-sfb-weyl-reflection-realization]. Also $n^2=h(-1)\in T$, and $nU_\alpha n^{-1}=U_{-\alpha}$. Replacing a chosen representative by $n$ changes no double coset, since representatives differ by $T(F)\subseteq B(K)$.

Write $B_K=B(K)$ and $U_\beta=U_\beta(K)$ in this and the next steps. By [lem-sfb-borel-root-product-coordinates] and $B=U\rtimes T$ from [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure], we may write $B_K=V U_\alpha T(K)$, where $V$ is the ordered product of the other positive root groups; no assertion that $V$ is a subgroup is needed. The first step shows $s$ permutes these other positive roots, so the preceding conjugation calculation gives $nVn^{-1}\subseteq B_K$. Consequently $$D_sD_w=B_K n B_K n_w B_K\subseteq B_K U_{-\alpha} n n_w B_K.$$ The reverse inclusion holds since $U_{-\alpha}=nU_\alpha n^{-1}$, whence every $u n$ with $u\in U_{-\alpha}$ lies in $nB_K$. This proves equality. The product is invariant under left and right multiplication by $B_K$, and contains $n n_w$, so it always contains $D_{sw}$.

source.place: Proposition 21.75 (T3), p.448; Theorem 21.68 and Remark 21.69, pp.445--446.

proof.text: Suppose $w^{-1}\alpha\in\Phi^+$. For $x=n n_w$, conjugating $U_{-\alpha}$ by $x^{-1}$ gives $U_{w^{-1}\alpha}\subseteq B_K$. Thus the previous equality becomes $$D_sD_w=B_K U_{-\alpha}xB_K=B_K xB_K=D_{sw}.$$ Here the containment of a positive root group in $B_K$ is exactly the positive-root inclusion of [lem-sfb-borel-root-product-coordinates]. By the length criterion this is the required increasing case.

Suppose $w^{-1}\alpha\in-\Phi^+$. For $a\ne0$, direct multiplication in $\operatorname{SL}_2(K)$ gives $$x_-(a)=x_+(a^{-1})\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&-1\\1&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)\operatorname{diag}(a,a^{-1})x_+(a^{-1}).$$ Apply [lem-sfb-opposite-root-sl2-parametrizations]. Since $u_+(a^{-1}),h(a)\in B_K$, $n$ normalizes $T$, $n^2\in T$, and $nU_\alpha n^{-1}=U_{-\alpha}$, it follows that $$u_-(a)n n_w\in B_K U_{-\alpha} n_w.$$ But $n_w^{-1}U_{-\alpha}n_w=U_{-w^{-1}\alpha}\subseteq B_K$, so this lies in $D_w$. For $a=0$ the element lies in $D_{sw}$. The parametrization $u_-:K\to U_{-\alpha}(K)$ is bijective. Therefore the product equality above yields $D_sD_w\subseteq D_{sw}\cup D_w$. It contains $D_{sw}$ already; taking $a=1$ supplies a point of $D_w$, and its left/right $B_K$ invariance supplies all of $D_w$. This proves equality and, by the length criterion, the decreasing case, in every characteristic.

source.place: Proposition 21.75 (T3), p.448, negative-root case; explicit SL2 identity repairs the omitted final w.

proof.text: For a reduced word $w=s_{i_1}\cdots s_{i_m}$, every suffix is reduced: otherwise a shorter suffix word prefixed by the same letters would shorten the original word. Induct on $m\ge1$. For $m=1$ the product is $D_w$ by definition. For $m>1$, the suffix $v=s_{i_2}\cdots s_{i_m}$ has length $m-1$ and its double-coset product equals $D_v$ by induction. Since $\ell(s_{i_1}v)=\ell(v)+1$, the increasing formula gives $D_{s_{i_1}}D_v=D_w$. Finally any representative $n_1$ lies in $T(F)$, so $D_1=B_K$. This specifies the empty-word convention as the identity of the algebra of $B_K$-bi-invariant subsets (namely $B_K$), without identifying it with the singleton identity in the full subset monoid. For the rank-zero group there are no simple reflections and only this last assertion remains.

source.place: Reduced-product consequence of Proposition 21.75, with explicit suffix induction.
